note: Curated themes: each list is a deliberate subset, not a sector renamed. The rule-based themes are computed on the client from the live data so they never go stale.

themes.label: AI & SEMICONDUCTORS
themes.note: Companies whose revenue depends on chipmaking or AI infrastructure — equipment, materials (including Ajinomoto’s build-up film for CPU substrates), memory, components and the platforms selling the compute.

themes.label: DEFENCE
themes.note: Prime-listed suppliers to Japan's defence budget expansion — platforms, engines, electronics and specialised components.

themes.label: TRADING HOUSES
themes.note: The sogo shosha: conglomerates that own stakes across energy, metals, food and machinery. They trade at a discount to book, return cash through dividends and buybacks, and are the market’s read on the reform story.

themes.label: AUTOS & TRANSPORT EQUIPMENT
themes.note: The world’s largest carmakers and the suppliers behind them. The yen sets the export margin, and the electric transition sets the multiple.

themes.label: BANKS & FINANCIALS
themes.note: Megabanks, regional banks and brokers. A rising policy rate widens the lending spread for the first time in two decades, which is the whole investment case.

themes.label: PHARMACEUTICALS
themes.note: Domestic drugmakers with ageing-portfolio exposure and a wave of patent expiries. Licensing deals and the US pipeline are what re-rate them.

themes.label: CONSUMER & RETAIL
themes.note: Food, beverages and the retail chains. Pricing power after years of deflation is the theme: the names that raised prices without losing volume are the ones that worked.

themes.label: MACHINERY & AUTOMATION
themes.note: Factory automation, robotics and heavy machinery. Orders from China and the US data-centre build-out are the two swing factors.
